function: Joint downlink power-splitting factors (RS common message) and power-control coefficients (private messages) of the AP precoders in cell-free massive MIMO, maximizing sum SE (pp. 4, 7-8).
system: Downlink rate-splitting cell-free massive MIMO: L APs with N-antenna ULAs, K single-antenna UEs (L=20, N=4, K=4 for GAI); no RIS; 2 GHz carrier (pp. 3, 9, 12).
method: Conditional denoising diffusion model (generative AI, T=10 denoising steps) mapping environment (Rician factor, ASD) to power solutions; supervised training on genetic-algorithm expert solutions (pp. 8-9).
data_channel: Custom simulated spatially correlated Rician fading (ULA LoS plus clustered NLoS) with three-slope path loss; APs and UEs uniform in a 500 m square (pp. 3, 9).
test_conditions: Trained on expert solutions over Rician factor (-10 to 20 dB) and ASD (5-90 degrees) grids; tested at grid points, same K=4, L=20, N=4 (pp. 9, 12).
baselines: Non-learned: without RS, RS with equal or heuristic statistical-CSI power allocation, genetic-algorithm expert/upper bound. Learned: PPO-based DRL [30] (pp. 10-12).
metrics: Sum spectral efficiency (bit/s/Hz): CDF and versus transmit power, initial power-splitting factor, number of APs, Rician factor, ASD, and training epoch (pp. 10-12).
complexity: Order O(N_gai(G + T w_a + w_c)) for the GAI algorithm versus O(N_drl(G + w_a + w_c)) for DRL; no runtime or parameter counts reported (p. 9).
q1_support: p. 3: "between UE k and AP l is modeled as Rician fading"; p. 9: "Utilizing the three-slope propagation model [1], [19], we consider a simulation environment". Custom spatially correlated Rician simulator; no 3GPP TR 38.901, COST 2100, DeepMIMO, or measured channel.
q2_support: p. 9: "We compute a small number of expert solutions for training and inference" over Rician factor -10 to 20 dB and ASD 5-90 degree grids; p. 12: Fig. 9 tests at -10 to 10 dB and 10-90 degrees, inside those grids, with the same K = 4, L = 20, N = 4. No unseen scenario or configuration.
q3_support: p. 12: "the sum SE gain from the GAI-based algorithm consistently exceeds twice that of the heuristic algorithm" (non-learned; Fig. 9 also shows without RS and the GA expert); p. 2: "compared with the DRL-based algorithm [30], our proposed GAI-based algorithm can smoothly and continuously converge to a better performance" (PPO DRL on sum SE, Fig. 8, p. 12).
q4_support: p. 9: "The complexity of our GAI-based algorithm can be expressed as O(Ngai (G+ T wa + wc ))".
q5_support: p. 9: "We compute a small number of expert solutions for training and inference" from the simulated Rician model; the paper gives no code or data link and uses no public channel dataset or measurements.
notes: Identity: the PDF is arXiv:2409.14702v2 (24 Sep 2024), 'Rate-Splitting for Cell-Free Massive MIMO: Performance Analysis and Generative AI Approach', Zheng et al.; the preprint prints no DOI, but title and authors are consistent with the TCOM article of this DOI. Area: the learned diffusion model outputs only the power part of the AP precoders (power-splitting rho_l between RS common and private streams, Eq. 14 p. 4, and per-AP power control eta_il), while precoder directions are fixed (MR private, superposition-based common, Theorem 1 p. 5); assigned area 3 as base-station precoder power design, reviewer to confirm against a 'function' exclusion (power allocation is not among the excluded functions). The closed-form SE, heuristics, and genetic algorithm (pp. 3-7) are non-learned; only Section IV (pp. 7-9) is learned. Method: training uses GA expert solutions with the denoising loss of Eqs. (40)-(41), p. 9; the complexity paragraph also mentions actor and critic networks [40]. q2: the paper claims 'strong generalization capabilities across different environments' (p. 12), but Fig. 9 test points (Rician factor -10..10 dB, ASD 10..90 degrees) lie on the training grids of p. 9 (1 dB and 5 degree steps), with the same network size. q3: Fig. 8 shows sum SE versus training epoch, PPO DRL plateauing near 10 bit/s/Hz versus about 16 bit/s/Hz for GAI, so the learned comparison is on the achieved sum SE, not convergence alone; DRL is not in Fig. 9. q4: order of complexity of training, with GA cost G ignored; hardware is listed (i7-12700H, RTX 3060, p. 9) but no runtime is reported.
